namespace Erdos586

/--
Is there a covering system such that no two of the moduli divide each other?

Asked by Schinzel, motivated by a question of Erdős and Selfridge (see
[7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)). The answer is no, as proved by Balister, Bollobás,
Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST22].

The moduli of a `CoveringSystem ℤ` are the ideals $(m_i)$; the modulus $m_i$ divides $m_j$
exactly when $(m_j)\subseteq (m_i)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at

theorem erdos_586 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ c : CoveringSystem ℤ, Pairwise fun i j ↦ ¬ c.moduli j ≤ c.moduli i := by
  sorry

end Erdos586

reformulations.difference: The Lean represents congruence classes using nonzero proper ideals of ℤ and expresses nondivisibility as an indexwise antichain under ideal containment. It uses CoveringSystem rather than explicitly requiring distinct or increasingly ordered numerical moduli.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every nonzero proper ideal of ℤ is uniquely (m) for a positive integer m ≥ 2. Membership in {a} + (m) is exactly congruence to a modulo m, and (m_j) ≤ (m_i) iff m_i divides m_j. Pairwise quantifies over all distinct indices, so the condition forbids divisibility in both directions and automatically excludes repeated moduli. A finite family can then be reordered increasingly. In scratch.lean, I proved the equivalence between the Lean existential and the usual finite arithmetic-congruence existential with natural moduli greater than 1 and pairwise nondivisibility.
